definitionEn: a place where you buy things
example: There is a small shop on the corner.

definitionEn: a large shop
example: The furniture store is outside town.

definitionEn: a large shop that sells food and household goods
example: We do the weekly shop at the supermarket.

definitionEn: a very large supermarket, often with parking
example: The hypermarket is cheaper but further away.

definitionEn: a small local shop, often open late
example: The corner shop sells milk after nine.

definitionEn: a table outdoors where a person sells goods
example: Buy strawberries from the market stall.

definitionEn: a market for old or second-hand things
example: You can find vintage clothes at the flea market.

definitionEn: a large indoor shopping centre
example: Teenagers hang out at the mall on Saturdays.

definitionEn: the main street in a town with shops
example: Most banks are on the high street.

definitionEn: a shop that sells last season's goods cheaper
example: We bought jackets at the outlet village.

definitionEn: a shop that sells books
example: The bookshop has a café upstairs.

definitionEn: a shop that sells clothes
example: This clothes shop has a sale this week.

definitionEn: a shop that sells shoes
example: The shoe shop will stretch tight boots.

definitionEn: a shop that sells sports clothes and equipment
example: I got a new football at the sports shop.

definitionEn: a shop that sells toys
example: The toy shop is busy before Christmas.

definitionEn: a shop that sells medicine and toiletries
example: Buy toothpaste at the chemist's.

definitionEn: a shop that tests eyes and sells glasses
example: I have an appointment at the optician's.

definitionEn: a shop that sells watches and jewellery
example: The jeweller's repairs broken watches.

definitionEn: a shop that cleans clothes you cannot wash at home
example: Take the coat to the dry cleaner's.

definitionEn: a service that mends shoes
example: Shoe repair on the high street is cheap.

definitionEn: a shop that books holidays
example: Book the trip at the travel agent's.

definitionEn: a shop that sells or rents houses
example: The estate agent's has photos of flats in the window.

definitionEn: a small shop at a place where cars buy fuel
example: The petrol station shop is open all night.

definitionEn: a machine that sells drinks or snacks after you put money in
example: The vending machine in the hall is broken.

definitionEn: the place in a supermarket where you pay
example: The checkout on the left is faster.

definitionEn: a machine where you scan and pay yourself
example: Use the self-service till if you have only a few items.

definitionEn: a small container you carry while you shop
example: Take a shopping basket, not a trolley.

definitionEn: a large basket on wheels in a supermarket
example: Put heavy bottles at the bottom of the trolley.

definitionEn: a bag from a shop, often plastic or paper
example: Bring a cloth bag instead of a carrier bag.

definitionEn: a shop card that gives points or discounts
example: Show your loyalty card to collect points.

definitionEn: a card with money on it to spend in a shop
example: I got a gift card for my birthday.

definitionEn: a ticket that gives you money off or a free item
example: This voucher is worth ten zloty.

definitionEn: a lower price for a short time
example: Pizza is on special offer this week.

definitionEn: a deal where you get two items but pay for one
example: Shampoo is two for one until Sunday.

definitionEn: costing 50 percent less than usual
example: The bread is half price after six.

definitionEn: sold for less because it will expire or is last season
example: Reduced sandwiches are by the door.

definitionEn: the date after which food may not taste as good
example: Check the best before date on the yoghurt.

definitionEn: the last date you should eat a product for safety
example: Do not eat chicken after the use by date.

definitionEn: the pattern of lines a scanner reads on a product
example: The bar code will not scan — type the number.

definitionEn: the paper on a product with name, price or size
example: Read the label for washing instructions.

definitionEn: a small label showing how much something costs
example: The price tag is still on the jacket.

definitionEn: the printed proof of payment from the till
example: Keep the till receipt for returns.

definitionEn: the secret number you type when you pay by card
example: Do not tell anyone your PIN.

definitionEn: paying by tapping a card or phone, without a PIN
example: Contactless is faster in a long queue.

definitionEn: a card that takes money straight from your bank account
example: I pay with a debit card, not cash.

definitionEn: paper money
example: The machine does not take notes, only coins.

definitionEn: metal money
example: I have no coins for the locker.

definitionEn: money you get back when you pay with too much
example: The cashier gave me the wrong change.

definitionEn: to let the seller keep extra money as a tip
example: Keep the change — it was only fifty groszy.

definitionEn: to ask for more money than the correct price
example: They overcharge tourists in that souvenir shop.

definitionEn: to ask for less money than the correct price
example: They undercharge us by two zloty by mistake.

definitionEn: a statement that something is wrong with goods or service
example: I made a complaint about the broken zip.

definitionEn: to say you are not satisfied
example: Complain to the manager, not the junior assistant.

definitionEn: the person in charge of a shop
example: I'd like to speak to the manager.

definitionEn: the place in a shop for returns and questions
example: Returns are at the customer service desk.

definitionEn: to take goods back to the shop
example: You can return unworn clothes within 14 days.

definitionEn: a promise to repair or replace a product if it breaks
example: The phone has a two-year guarantee.

definitionEn: a written promise that a product will work for a period
example: The warranty does not cover water damage.

definitionEn: not working correctly
example: This charger is faulty — it gets hot.

definitionEn: not in the shop at the moment
example: Size 38 is out of stock until next week.

definitionEn: available to buy now
example: Is the blue model in stock?

definitionEn: with no items left to sell
example: Concert T-shirts are sold out.

definitionEn: a request to buy goods; to make that request
example: I will order the book online.

definitionEn: buying on the internet and picking up in a shop
example: Click and collect is ready in two hours.

definitionEn: when a shop brings goods to your house
example: Home delivery is free over 100 zloty.

definitionEn: to follow where a package is on its way to you
example: You can track a parcel with this number.

definitionEn: a person or company that delivers parcels
example: The courier rang twice and left a card.

definitionEn: the money you pay to send a letter or parcel
example: Postage to Britain is expensive.

definitionEn: a small paper you stick on a letter to pay for sending it
example: You need a stamp for this postcard.

definitionEn: something wrapped to send in the post
example: A parcel from grandma arrived today.

definitionEn: to start a bank account
example: You can open an account at sixteen with a parent.

definitionEn: money you keep for later
example: I put my savings in the bank.

definitionEn: to give money that must be given back
example: I can lend you five zloty until Friday.

definitionEn: to take money that you must pay back
example: Do not borrow money if you cannot pay it back.

definitionEn: to need to pay money back to someone
example: You still owe me for the cinema ticket.

definitionEn: to have no money (informal)
example: I will be broke until pocket money day.

definitionEn: to keep money until you have enough to buy something
example: I save up for a new bike.

definitionEn: to spend a lot of money on something you want
example: Do not splash out on clothes every week.

definitionEn: a purchase at a fair or low price
example: That laptop was a good deal in the sale.

definitionEn: something that costs far too much (informal)
example: Four zloty for a bottle of water is a rip-off.

definitionEn: to compare prices in different shops before you buy
example: Shop around before you buy a phone.

definitionEn: to look at goods without a plan to buy at once
example: We just want to browse, thank you.

definitionEn: to go in front of people who were waiting first
example: It is rude to queue-jump.

definitionEn: the times when a shop is open
example: Check the opening hours for Sunday.

definitionEn: not open for customers
example: The post office is closed on Saturday afternoon.

definitionEn: open all day and all night
example: The garage shop is open 24 hours.

definitionEn: a small room in a clothes shop for trying clothes on
example: The fitting room is at the back.
